sanskrit: sthāṇur uvāca prajāsarganimittaṃ me kāryavattām imāṃ prabho viddhi sṛṣṭās tvayā hīmā mā kupyāsāṃ pitāmaha
english: Sthāṇu said: Know, O lord, that this duty laid upon me concerns the bringing forth of creatures. These beings were created by you, O grandsire; do not be angry with them.

sanskrit: tava tejogninā deva prajā dahyanti sarvaśaḥ tā dṛṣṭvā mama kāruṇyaṃ mā kupyāsāṃ jagatprabho
english: By the fire of your splendour, O god, the creatures are being consumed on every side. Seeing them, compassion stirs in me. Be not wrathful, O lord of the world.

sanskrit: prajāpatir uvāca na kupye na ca me kāmo na bhaveran prajā iti lāghavārthaṃ dharaṇyās tu tataḥ saṃhāra iṣyate
english: Prajāpati said: I am not angry, nor is it my wish that the creatures should cease to be. It is only to lighten the burden of the earth that I will their destruction.

sanskrit: iyaṃ hi māṃ sadā devī bhārārtā samacodayat saṃhārārthaṃ mahādeva bhāreṇāpsu nimajjati
english: For this goddess Earth, oppressed by her load, has ever urged me to it, O Mahādeva. Burdened, she sinks down into the waters.

sanskrit: yadāhaṃ nādhigacchāmi buddhyā bahu vicārayan saṃhāram āsāṃ vṛddhānāṃ tato māṃ krodha āviśat
english: When, pondering long with my mind, I could find no means for the destruction of these multiplied beings, then anger entered into me.

sanskrit: sthāṇur uvāca saṃhārāntaṃ prasīdasva mā krudhas tridaśeśvara mā prajāḥ sthāvaraṃ vaica jaṅgamaṃ ca vinīnaśaḥ
english: Sthāṇu said: Let go your purpose of destruction and be appeased; be not wrathful, O lord of the thirty gods. Do not annihilate the creatures, neither what stands fixed nor what moves.

sanskrit: palvalāni ca sarvāṇi sarvaṃ caiva tṛṇolapam sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caiva bhūtagrāmaṃ caturvidham
english: All the pools, and all the grasses and reeds, the fixed and the moving alike — the whole fourfold host of living beings —

sanskrit: tad etad bhasmasād bhūtaṃ jagat sarvam upaplutam prasīda bhagavan sādho vara eṣa vṛto mayā
english: all this is being reduced to ashes; the entire world is overwhelmed. Be gracious, O blessed and holy one — this is the boon I crave of you.

sanskrit: naṣṭā na punar eṣyanti prajā hy etāḥ kathaṃ cana tasmān nivartyatām etat tejaḥ svenaiva tejasā
english: For these creatures, once destroyed, will by no means come again. Therefore let this splendour be withdrawn by your own splendour.

sanskrit: upāyam anyaṃ saṃpaśya prajānāṃ hitakāmyayā yatheme jantavaḥ sarve nivarteran paraṃtapa
english: Look to some other means, out of desire for the creatures' welfare, by which all these living beings may be turned back, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: abhāvam abhigaccheyur utsannaprajanāḥ prajāḥ adhidaivaniyukto 'smi tvayā lokeṣv iheśvara
english: Else the creatures, their power of generation cut off, would pass into non-being. I have been appointed by you, O lord, to preside over the divine ordering of the worlds here.

sanskrit: tvad bhavaṃ hi jagannātha jagat sthāvarajaṅgamam prasādya tvāṃ mahādeva yācāmy āvṛttijāḥ prajāḥ
english: For this world of the fixed and the moving has its origin in you, O lord of the world. Having appeased you, O Mahādeva, I beg for the creatures that they be reborn again and again.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca śrutvā tu vacanaṃ devaḥ sthāṇor niyatavāṅmanāḥ tejas tat svaṃ nijagrāha punar evāntar ātmanā
english: Nārada said: Hearing the words of Sthāṇu, the god, his speech and mind restrained, drew that splendour of his back once more within his own self.

sanskrit: tato 'gnim upasaṃgṛhya bhagavāṃl lokapūjitaḥ pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca kalpayām āsa vai prabhuḥ
english: Then, gathering in that fire, the blessed lord, honoured by the worlds, ordained both the going forth into activity and the turning back from it.

sanskrit: upasaṃharatas tasya tam agniṃ roṣajaṃ tadā prādurbabhūva viśvebhyaḥ khebhyo nārī mahātmanaḥ
english: As the great-souled one was drawing back that fire born of his wrath, there appeared from all the openings of his body a woman.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇā raktāmbaradharā raktanetratalāntarā divyakuṇḍalasaṃpannā divyābharaṇabhūṣitā
english: Dark she was, clad in red garments, the corners of her eyes tinged red within, furnished with divine earrings and adorned with celestial ornaments.

sanskrit: sā viniḥsṛtya vai khebhyo dakṣiṇām āśritā diśam dadṛśāte 'tha tau kanyāṃ devau viśveśvarāv ubhau
english: Having issued forth from those openings, she betook herself to the southern quarter. Then the two gods, both lords of the universe, beheld that maiden.

sanskrit: tām āhūya tadā devo lokānām ādir īśvaraḥ mṛtyo iti mahīpāla jahi cemāḥ prajā iti
english: Then the god, the first lord of the worlds, calling her, said — O protector of earth — "O Death, slay these creatures."

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi saṃhārabuddhyā me cintitā ruṣitena ca tasmāt saṃhara sarvās tvaṃ prajāḥ sajaḍapaṇḍitāḥ
english: "For you were conceived by me in my wrath, with my mind set upon destruction. Therefore destroy you all the creatures, the foolish and the wise alike.

sanskrit: aviśeṣeṇa caiva tvaṃ prajāḥ saṃhara bhāmini mama tvaṃ hi niyogena śreyaḥ param avāpsyasi
english: Without distinction, O lovely one, do you destroy the creatures. By performing this my charge, you shall attain the highest good."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu sā devī mṛtyuḥ kamalamālinī pradadhyau duḥkhitā bālā sāśrupātam atīva hi
english: Thus addressed, the goddess Death, garlanded with lotuses, that young maiden, sank into grieving thought, sorrowful, the tears falling fast from her eyes.

sanskrit: pāṇibhyāṃ caiva jagrāha tāny aśrūṇi janeśvaraḥ mānavānāṃ hitārthāya yayāce punar eva ca
english: And the lord of beings caught up those tears in his two hands, and, for the good of mortals, entreated her once again.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca vinīya duḥkham abalā sā tv atīvāyatekṣaṇā uvāca prāñjalir bhūtvā latevāvarjitā tadā
english: Nārada said: Putting away her grief, that gentle one of long, far-reaching eyes, with palms joined and bowing low like a creeper bent down, then spoke.

sanskrit: tvayā sṛṣṭā kathaṃ nārī mādṛśī vadatāṃ vara raudrakarmābhijāyeta sarvaprāṇibhayaṃkarī
english: "How, O best of speakers, should a woman such as I, created by you, come to be born to so dread a work, terrible to every living thing?

sanskrit: bibhemy aham adharmasya dharmyam ādiśa karma me tvaṃ māṃ bhītām avekṣasva śiveneśvara cakṣuṣā
english: I am afraid of unrighteousness. Appoint me to a righteous task. Look upon me in my fear, O lord, with a kindly eye.

sanskrit: bālān vṛddhān vayaḥsthāṃś ca na hareyam anāgasaḥ prāṇinaḥ prāṇinām īśa namas te 'bhiprasīda me
english: That I should not carry off the guiltless living — children, the aged, those in the prime of life — O lord of all that breathes, I bow to you: be gracious to me.

sanskrit: priyān putrān vayasyāṃś ca bhrātṝn mātṝḥ pitṝn api apadhyāsyanti yad deva mṛtāṃs teṣāṃ bibhemy aham
english: Beloved sons, friends, brothers, mothers, and fathers too — that men should brood upon these when dead, O god, of that I am afraid.

sanskrit: kṛpaṇāśruparikledo dahen māṃ śāśvatīḥ samāḥ tebhyo 'haṃ balavad bhītā śaraṇaṃ tvām upāgatā
english: The flood of their piteous tears would scald me through endless years. Sorely afraid of them, I have come to you for refuge.

sanskrit: yamasya bhavane deva yāty ante pāpakarmiṇaḥ prasādaye tvā varada prasādaṃ kuru me prabho
english: To the house of Yama, O god, the doer of evil deeds goes at the last. I beseech you, O giver of boons: show me your grace, O lord.

sanskrit: etam icchāmy ahaṃ kāmaṃ tvatto lokapitāmaha iccheyaṃ tvatprasādāc ca tapas taptuṃ sureśvara
english: This is the boon I desire of you, O grandsire of the worlds; and by your grace I would wish to practise austerities, O lord of the gods."

sanskrit: pitāmaha uvāca mṛtyo saṃkalpitā me tvaṃ prajāsaṃhārahetunā gaccha saṃhara sarvās tvaṃ prajā mā ca vicāraya
english: The grandsire said: O Death, you were fashioned by me for the very purpose of destroying the creatures. Go, destroy you all the creatures, and do not hesitate.

sanskrit: etad evam avaśyaṃ hi bhavitā naitad anyathā kriyatām anavadyāṅgi yathoktaṃ madvaco 'naghe
english: This must inevitably come to pass; it cannot be otherwise. Do as I have said, O faultless-limbed and sinless one — fulfil my word.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca evam uktā mahābāho mṛtyuḥ parapuraṃjaya na vyājahāra tasthau ca prahvā bhagavadunmukhī
english: Nārada said: Thus addressed, O mighty-armed conqueror of hostile cities, Death made no reply, but stood bowed down, her face turned up toward the lord.

sanskrit: punaḥ punar athoktā sā gatasattveva bhāminī tūṣṇīm āsīt tato devo devānām īśvareśvaraḥ
english: Though addressed again and again, that fair one stood silent, as though her very life had gone from her. Then the god, the supreme lord of the gods,

sanskrit: prasasāda kila brahmā svayam evātmanātmavān smayamānaś ca lokeśo lokān sarvān avaikṣata
english: Brahmā, self-possessed, was of himself appeased; and smiling, the lord of the worlds looked out upon all the worlds.

sanskrit: nivṛttaroṣe tasmiṃs tu bhagavaty aparājite sā kanyāpajagāmāsya samīpād iti naḥ śrutam
english: And when that unconquered and blessed one had laid aside his wrath, the maiden slipped away from his presence — so have we heard.

sanskrit: apasṛtyāpratiśrutya prajāsaṃharaṇaṃ tadā tvaramāṇeva rājendra mṛtyur dhenukam abhyayāt
english: Having withdrawn without consenting to the destruction of the creatures, Death then, as if in haste, O king of kings, went off to Dhenuka.

sanskrit: sā tatra paramaṃ devī tapo 'carata duścaram samā hy ekapade tasthau daśa padmāni pañca ca
english: There the goddess practised supreme and hard austerity: she stood upon one foot for fifteen padmas of years.

sanskrit: tāṃ tathā kurvatīṃ tatra tapaḥ paramaduścaram punar eva mahātejā brahmā vacanam abravīt
english: As she was thus performing her exceedingly hard austerity there, the mighty-splendoured Brahmā once again spoke these words:

sanskrit: kuruṣva me vaco mṛtyo tad anādṛtya satvarā tathaivaikapade tāta punar anyāni sapta sā
english: "Carry out my word, O Death." Disregarding it, she swiftly stood again upon one foot for yet another seven —

sanskrit: tasthau padmāni ṣaṭ caiva pañca dve caiva mānada bhūyaḥ padmāyutaṃ tāta mṛgaiḥ saha cacāra sā
english: she stood for six padmas, and five, and two, O bestower of honour; and then for ten thousand padmas more she ranged about in the company of deer.

sanskrit: punar gatvā tato rājan maunam ātiṣṭhad uttamam apsu varṣasahasrāṇi sapta caikaṃ ca pārthiva
english: Then going off again, O king, she kept the most exalted silence within the waters for eight thousand years, O ruler of earth.

sanskrit: tato jagāma sā kanyā kauśikīṃ bharatarṣabha tatra vāyujalāhārā cacāra niyamaṃ punaḥ
english: Then that maiden went to the Kauśikī, O bull of the Bhāratas; and there, feeding on wind and water, she again practised her vow.

sanskrit: tato yayau mahābhāgā gaṅgāṃ meruṃ ca kevalam tasthau dārv iva niśceṣṭā bhūtānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: Then the greatly blessed one went on to the Gaṅgā and to lonely Meru, and stood there motionless as a log, out of her desire for the good of living beings.

sanskrit: tato himavato mūrdhni yatra devāḥ samījire tatrāṅguṣṭhena rājendra nikharvam aparaṃ tataḥ tasthau pitāmahaṃ caiva toṣayām āsa yatnataḥ
english: Then on the summit of Himavat, where the gods had performed their sacrifices, there she stood upon her great toe, O king of kings, for yet another nikharva of years, and with effort she gratified the grandsire.

sanskrit: tatas tām abravīt tatra lokānāṃ prabhavāpyayaḥ kim idaṃ vartate putri kriyatāṃ tad vaco mama
english: Then He who is the origin and the dissolution of the worlds said to her there: "What is this you do, my daughter? Let my word be carried out."

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt punar mṛtyur bhagavantaṃ pitāmaham na hareyaṃ prajā deva punas tvāhaṃ prasādaye
english: Then Death spoke again to the blessed grandsire: "I would not carry off the creatures, O god; once more I beseech your grace."

sanskrit: tām adharmabhayatrastāṃ punar eva ca yācatīm tadābravīd devadevo nigṛhyedaṃ vacas tataḥ
english: To her, trembling with the fear of unrighteousness and entreating him yet again, the god of gods then spoke these words, restraining her resolve:

sanskrit: adharmo nāsti te mṛtyo saṃyacchemāḥ prajāḥ śubhe mayā hy uktaṃ mṛṣā bhadre bhavitā neha kiṃ cana
english: "There is no unrighteousness for you, O Death. Gather in these creatures, O fair one. What I have spoken, O blessed lady, shall not in any way prove false here.

sanskrit: dharmaḥ sanātanaś ca tvām ihaivānupravekṣyate ahaṃ ca vibudhāś caiva tvaddhite niratāḥ sadā
english: The eternal Law itself shall enter into you here; and I and the gods shall ever be intent upon your welfare.

sanskrit: imam anyaṃ ca te kāmaṃ dadāmi manasepsitam na tvā doṣeṇa yāsyanti vyādhisaṃpīḍitāḥ prajāḥ
english: And this further boon, desired in your heart, I grant you: the creatures, afflicted by disease, shall not come to you charged with any fault of yours.

sanskrit: puruṣeṣu ca rūpeṇa puruṣas tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi strīṣu strīrūpiṇī caiva tṛtīyeṣu napuṃsakam
english: Among men you shall be a man in form, among women a woman in shape, and among the third sort a being of neither kind."

sanskrit: saivam uktā mahārāja kṛtāñjalir uvāca ha punar eva mahātmānaṃ neti deveśam avyayam
english: Thus addressed, O great king, she spoke with joined palms once more to that great-souled and imperishable lord of the gods, saying, "No":

sanskrit: tām abravīt tadā devo mṛtyo saṃhara mānavān adharmas te na bhavitā tathā dhyāsyāmy ahaṃ śubhe
english: Then the god said to her: "O Death, gather in the race of men. No unrighteousness shall touch you; so will I ordain it, O fair one.

sanskrit: yān aśrubindūn patitān apaśyaṃ; ye pāṇibhyāṃ dhāritās te purastāt te vyādhayo mānavān ghorarūpāḥ; prāpte kāle pīḍayiṣyanti mṛtyo
english: Those drops of tears that I saw fallen, which were caught and held in my two hands before — those, O Death, shall become diseases of dreadful form, and when the time comes they shall torment mankind.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ tvaṃ prāṇinām antakāle; kāmakrodhau sahitau yojayethāḥ evaṃ dharmas tvām upaiṣyaty ameyo; na cādharmaṃ lapsyase tulyavṛttiḥ
english: At the last hour of all living beings you shall join desire and anger together upon them. Thus measureless Law shall come to you, and, dealing evenly with all, you shall incur no unrighteousness.

sanskrit: evaṃ dharmaṃ pālayiṣyasy athoktaṃ; na cātmānaṃ majjayiṣyasy adharme tasmāt kāmaṃ rocayābhyāgataṃ tvaṃ; saṃyojyātho saṃharasveha jantūn
english: Thus you shall guard the Law as I have declared it, and you shall not plunge yourself into sin. Therefore welcome the office that has come to you, and, joining these together, gather in the living beings here."

sanskrit: sā vai tadā mṛtyusaṃjñāpadeśāc; chāpād bhītā bāḍham ity abravīt tam atho prāṇān prāṇinām antakāle; kāmakrodhau prāpya nirmohya hanti
english: Then she, for fear of a curse and under the name and charge of Death, said to him, "So be it." And thereafter, at the last hour of living beings, taking hold of desire and anger, she bereaves them of delusion and slays them.

sanskrit: mṛtyor ye te vyādhayaś cāśrupātā; manuṣyāṇāṃ rujyate yaiḥ śarīram sarveṣāṃ vai prāṇināṃ prāṇanānte; tasmāc chokaṃ mā kṛthā budhya buddhyā
english: Those diseases of Death, born of her falling tears, by which the bodies of men are racked — they come at the ending of the breath of all that lives. Therefore grieve not, but understand this with your understanding.

sanskrit: sarve devāḥ prāṇināṃ prāṇanānte; gatvā vṛttāḥ saṃnivṛttās tathaiva evaṃ sarve mānavāḥ prāṇanānte; gatvāvṛttā devavad rājasiṃha
english: All the gods, at the ending of the breath of living beings, having gone forth, return again even so; and so too all men, at the ending of their breath, having gone, return like gods, O lion among kings.

sanskrit: vāyur bhīmo bhīmanādo mahaujāḥ; sarveṣāṃ ca prāṇināṃ prāṇabhūtaḥ nānāvṛttir dehināṃ dehabhede; tasmād vāyur devadevo viśiṣṭaḥ
english: The Wind, dread and dreadful-voiced, of mighty power, is the very life-breath of all living things; he takes manifold courses when the bodies of the embodied break apart. Therefore the Wind is the god of gods, supreme.

sanskrit: sarve devā martyasaṃjñāviśiṣṭāḥ; sarve martyā devasaṃjñāviśiṣṭāḥ tasmāt putraṃ mā śuco rājasiṃha; putraḥ svargaṃ prāpya te modate ha
english: All the gods are marked out by the name of mortal, and all mortals are marked out by the name of god. Therefore mourn not your son, O lion among kings: your son, having attained heaven, rejoices there.

sanskrit: evaṃ mṛtyur devasṛṣṭā prajānāṃ; prāpte kāle saṃharantī yathāvat tasyāś caiva vyādhayas te 'śrupātāḥ; prāpte kāle saṃharantīha jantūn
english: Thus Death, created by the god, gathers in the creatures duly when their time has come; and those diseases of hers, born of her tears, when the time has come, gather in the living beings here.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ime vai mānavāḥ sarve dharmaṃ prati viśaṅkitāḥ ko 'yaṃ dharmaḥ kuto dharmas tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: All these men are perplexed concerning the Law. What is this Law? Whence is the Law? Tell me that, O grandsire.

sanskrit: dharmo nv ayam ihārthaḥ kim amutrārtho 'pi vā bhavet ubhayārtho 'pi vā dharmas tan me brūhi pitāmaha
english: Is this Law for the sake of this world, or rather for the sake of the next? Or may the Law serve both ends? Tell me that, O grandsire.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sadācāraḥ smṛtir vedās trividhaṃ dharmalakṣaṇam caturtham artham ity āhuḥ kavayo dharmalakṣaṇam
english: Bhīṣma said: Right conduct, the Smṛti, and the Vedas — these are the threefold mark of the Law; and the wise declare profit, the fourth, to be a mark of the Law as well.

sanskrit: api hy uktāni karmāṇi vyavasyanty uttarāvare lokayātrārtham eveha dharmasya niyamaḥ kṛtaḥ ubhayatra sukhodarka iha caiva paratra ca
english: Though the rites be already prescribed, men later and former still resolve upon them. It is for the sustaining of worldly life that the rule of Law has here been laid down — a rule that ripens into happiness in both spheres, here and hereafter.

sanskrit: alabdhvā nipuṇaṃ dharmaṃ pāpaḥ pāpe prasajjati na ca pāpakṛtaḥ pāpān mucyante ke cid āpadi
english: Failing to grasp the subtle Law, the wicked man cleaves to sin; nor do certain doers of evil escape from sin even in time of distress.

sanskrit: apāpavādī bhavati yadā bhavati dharmavit dharmasya niṣṭhā svācāras tam evāśritya bhotsyase
english: When a man becomes a knower of the Law, he speaks no evil. Good conduct is the very ground of the Law; resting upon that alone, you shall come to understand it.

sanskrit: yadādharmasamāviṣṭo dhanaṃ gṛhṇāti taskaraḥ ramate nirharan stenaḥ paravittam arājake
english: When, possessed by unrighteousness, the thief seizes wealth, the robber takes delight in carrying off another's riches where there is no king.

sanskrit: yadāsya tad dharanty anye tadā rājānam icchati tadā teṣāṃ spṛhayate ye vai tuṣṭāḥ svakair dhanaiḥ
english: But when others carry off that wealth of his, then he longs for a king; and then he envies those who are content with their own riches.

sanskrit: abhītaḥ śucir abhyeti rājadvāram aśaṅkitaḥ na hi duścaritaṃ kiṃ cid antarātmani paśyati
english: The pure man approaches the king's gate unafraid and without misgiving, for he sees no misdeed of any kind within his own inmost self.

sanskrit: satyasya vacanaṃ sādhu na satyād vidyate param satyena vidhṛtaṃ sarvaṃ sarvaṃ satye pratiṣṭhitam
english: The utterance of truth is good; there is nothing higher than truth. By truth is all upheld; upon truth does all stand established.

sanskrit: api pāpakṛto raudrāḥ satyaṃ kṛtvā pṛthak pṛthak adroham avisaṃvādaṃ pravartante tadāśrayāḥ te cen mitho 'dhṛtiṃ kuryur vinaśyeyur asaṃśayam
english: Even fierce doers of evil, having pledged the truth among themselves each by each, proceed without treachery and without breach of faith, relying upon it; for were they to act faithlessly toward one another, they would assuredly perish.

sanskrit: na hartavyaṃ paradhanam iti dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ manyante balavantas taṃ durbalaiḥ saṃpravartitam yadā niyatidaurbalyam athaiṣām eva rocate
english: "Another's wealth is not to be taken" — this is the eternal Law. Yet the strong hold that it was set going by the weak; but when their own weakness is fixed upon them by fate, then that very Law pleases them.

sanskrit: na hy atyantaṃ balayutā bhavanti sukhino 'pi vā tasmād anārjave buddhir na kāryā te kathaṃ cana
english: For those who are endowed with strength are not therefore happy without end. Therefore let your mind in no wise be turned toward crookedness.

sanskrit: asādhubhyo 'sya na bhayaṃ na corebhyo na rājataḥ na kiṃ cit kasya cit kurvan nirbhayaḥ śucir āvaset
english: He has no fear from the wicked, nor from thieves, nor from the king. Doing wrong to no one in any thing, the pure man dwells without fear.

sanskrit: sarvataḥ śaṅkate steno mṛgo grāmam iveyivān bahudhācaritaṃ pāpam anyatraivānupaśyati
english: The thief is suspicious of everything, like a deer that has strayed into a village; the sin he himself has done in many ways he sees only in others.

sanskrit: muditaḥ śucir abhyeti sarvato nirbhayaḥ sadā na hi duścaritaṃ kiṃ cid ātmano 'nyeṣu paśyati
english: The pure man goes forward glad, ever fearless on every side, for he sees no misdeed of his own reflected in others.

sanskrit: dātavyam ity ayaṃ dharma ukto bhūtahite rataiḥ taṃ manyante dhanayutāḥ kṛpaṇaiḥ saṃpravartitam
english: "One ought to give" — this Law has been declared by those devoted to the good of all beings; but the wealthy hold that it was set going by the destitute.
